about.intro: {{name}} is the civic center for reading, literacy, and community enrichment in Garbaharey, Gedo. Discover diverse perspectives, study in quiet spaces, and explore thousands of books.
about.builtText1: A library starts with a collection, but it comes to life through the people who read it. Our website makes that collection easier to explore and helps you keep track of what you want to read next.

story.title: Our Story: Background and Development
story.p1: Garbaharey Public Library was established in Garbaharey, the historic capital of the Gedo region in Jubaland, Somalia. The library was born from a grassroots civic initiative led by local educators, community elders, and youth who recognized the urgent need for a dedicated learning sanctuary and accessible textbooks.
story.p2: Beginning with modest book donations, volunteer literacy drives, and community reading circles, the library steadily developed into a structured public institution. Over the years, it expanded its reading halls, cataloged thousands of physical volumes across diverse subjects, and introduced digital systems to serve modern readers.
story.p3: Today, Garbaharey Public Library stands as an enduring pillar of civic pride, providing barrier-free access to knowledge, safeguarding Somali literature and oral history, and inspiring future generations of students, researchers, and families.
story.milestone1Text: Local educators and community leaders gather the initial collection and open a reading circle.
story.milestone2Text: Dedicated reading rooms, reference stacks, and student study carrels established on Main Street.
story.milestone3Text: Launch of online OPAC cataloging, digitized inventory, and structured borrowing memberships.
story.milestone4Text: Ongoing literacy programs, youth reading marathons, and Somali cultural preservation.

director.title: Director’s Message
director.name: Dahir Mohamed Ali
director.quote: “Waxaan si diirran ugu soo dhawaynayaa qof kasta oo jecel akhriska iyo aqoonta Maktabadda Dadweynaha ee Garbahaareey. Knowledge is the foundation of individual dignity and community progress.”
director.message: On behalf of the staff, librarians, and advisory board of Garbaharey Public Library, it is my sincere honor to welcome you to our shared home of learning. A library is far more than shelves of books—it is the beating heart of our community, a quiet sanctuary for deep inquiry, and an equalizer of opportunity. Whether you are a student preparing for examinations, an educator researching curriculum materials, or a curious reader discovering new stories, our dedicated team is here to support you every step of the way. Welcome to your library.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.statement: To empower our community by providing open and equitable access to educational resources, fostering a culture of reading and literacy, and preserving Somali oral and written heritage for all generations in Garbaharey and the Gedo region.
mission.p1: Foster early literacy and lifelong learning habits across all ages.
mission.p2: Provide equitable, barrier-free access to literature and study facilities.
mission.p3: Preserve and promote Somali literature, poetry, and cultural history.
mission.p4: Support students and educators with verified academic references.

vision.title: Our Vision
vision.statement: To be the leading regional center of learning, cultural enrichment, and knowledge innovation in southwestern Somalia—inspiring an educated, enlightened, and self-reliant society.
vision.p1: Expand physical and digital collections across Somali, Arabic, and English.
vision.p2: Establish modern digital access labs and youth literacy programs.
vision.p3: Broaden educational outreach to schools throughout Gedo district.
vision.p4: Maintain an authoritative public archive of regional history and culture.

contact.faq1Q: Who can get a library card at Garbaharey Public Library?
contact.faq1A: Library cards are free and open to all residents, students, teachers, and community members in Garbaharey and surrounding Gedo districts.
contact.faq2Q: How long can I borrow books for, and can I renew them?
contact.faq2A: Standard loans are for 14 days. You can easily renew your books online via your member account or in person at the circulation desk if no other member has placed a hold.
contact.faq3Q: Are reading and study rooms free to use?
contact.faq3A: Yes, our reading halls and study desks are completely free and open to all visitors during regular operating hours without any reservation fee.
contact.faq4Q: Can school groups arrange private study visits?
contact.faq4A: Yes! Teachers and school groups can contact us in advance using the contact form or phone to arrange guided library visits and reserved group study areas.

questions.question: How do I become a member?
questions.answer: Open Join the Library, fill in the short form and submit it. Library staff review each application and you will be told when it is approved. You can also create an account yourself from the Sign in page.

questions.question: How do I borrow a book?
questions.answer: Find a title in the catalog and open its details. Sign in to reserve it, then arrange collection with library staff. Staff issue a specific physical copy and record its due date.

questions.question: Does a reservation guarantee immediate collection?
questions.answer: A reservation joins the queue for a title. When a copy is free, the first reader in the queue is told it is ready. Track your reservations in your member portal.

questions.question: What is the difference between saving and reserving?
questions.answer: Saving adds a title to your personal reading list. It does not reserve a copy. Reserving records a request to borrow a title when a copy is available for you.

questions.question: Can I renew a loan?
questions.answer: Open My Books in your member portal and select Renew. A loan cannot be renewed if it is overdue, has reached the renewal limit, or has a waiting reservation.

questions.question: How do I return a book or cancel a request?
questions.answer: Return physical copies to library staff so they can record the return. To cancel a reservation, open Reservations in your member portal and select Cancel.

questions.question: What happens if a book is overdue?
questions.answer: Overdue loans appear in your account. Please return the books or speak to library staff. New borrowing is blocked while you have overdue loans, and a fine may apply if the library has set one.

questions.question: Where can I see updates about my loans?
questions.answer: Open Notifications in your member portal for borrowing and reservation updates. With a verified email address, the library can also send reminders when email delivery is enabled.

process.title: How to Access Our Services
process.lead: Three straightforward steps to make the most of Garbaharey Public Library.
process.step1Text: Sign up online or visit our circulation desk on Main Street with identification to receive your official library card.
process.step2Text: Use our online catalog or browse our open shelves to explore titles, read summaries, and check copy availability.
process.step3Text: Take books home, read in our quiet reading halls, or join community literacy programs and workshops.
